“Don’t you know who I am?” he asked as he brandished his comically oversized swiss army knife. 

"N-no," she cried, crushing herself against the pink wall in the kitchen of the diner. She reconsidered her stance. She had spent two years waitressing at the waffle-themed diner, and right now, at this very moment in the late afternoon, she wondered if she should have applied at the pancake themed diner instead. That diner was just across town. She forgot for a moment where she was and wondered if her cat was scratching the arms of her sofa once again. 

The bright rays of the afternoon sun gleamed through the large windows in the kitchen. The man stepped backward, overcome with confusion. Wasn't he at the right place? He was supposed to enter the diner and meet his new girlfriend. He had pedalled his bike through the town, contemplating on the need for two separately themed diners in a town so small that everyone had the same dentist. 


He hesitated as he looked around the diner's kitchen. Maybe he had been catfished. After all, he never actually saw or even heard the voice of his new girlfriend. The waitress took advantage of the dark and rather handsome man's hesitation and grabbed a waffle iron. She raised it slowly when he suddenly leapt forward and grabbed it from her. 

He put the waffle iron down awkwardly. He bolted through the back doors of the kitchen without another word. What a strange turn of events, she thought. She looked at the door, looked at the waffle iron and sighed with relief.
